learning_outcomes.text: Introduction. General operations with information provided by database systems.
E - R conceptual model. Limitations for relations defined in DBS.
Models of Database System Management. Relational database systems. Codd, Characteristics (rules) for relational database systems. Set and relation operations in relational database system.
Architectures of Database System Management in personal computers. Systems "client/server".
Database application program languages. Structured language - SQL.
Programming in the system MS Access.
Programming in the system of ORACLE-type.
Data-based and Knowledge-Based systems. Operations with knowledge. Decision and Control paradigms. Operations with uncertainties. Theory of fuzzy sets.
Operations with fuzzy sets. Fuzzy numbers and computing with fuzzy numbers. Linguistic variable.
Fuzzy logic. Compositional rule and fuzzy inference. Types of fuzzy implications and their properties.
Types and kinds of knowledge representation. Expert system - modular structure. Inference engine and its co-operations with knowledge-base. System ETS.
Expert systems - examples (FELExpert, TRACER, XCON/XSELL, KEE, NEST, G2).
Future of database and knowledge systems. Conclusions of lectures.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. General operations with information provided in database systems.
E - R diagrams, relational diagrams. Integrity constraints for relationships defined in the DBS.
RDBMS models. Relational database systems. Client/server systems. Codd's rules for relational DBMS. Set and relational operations in a relational database system.
Database application programming languages. Structured query language - SQL.
Classic database programs for personal computers. Client/server systems, work with MS Access.
Simple database applications on the web: Forms, php language.
Simple database applications on the web: A simple application.
Fuzzy sets. Fuzzy set operations. Fuzzyfication and computing with fuzzy variables.
Fuzzy logic. Use of fuzzy logic.
Html generated from an SQL server response.
Testing of semester tasks. Conclusion of the semester.
